✨ AnyPS5 | C++
🎯 Primary Use Case: Porting PlayStation 5 games and applications to run on PC (Linux and Windows) without emulation.
✨ Key Features: • Automatic porting of PS5 executables to Linux and Windows • Relinker for converting executables to native formats • Implementations of system PRX libraries for dynamic linking • No emulation or separate runtime process required • Shader recompilation to SPIR-V
📖 Summary: AnyPS5 is a tool designed to automatically port PlayStation 5 executables to Linux and Windows. It achieves this by relinking the executables to the target system's native format and providing implementations of system PRX libraries for dynamic linking, without requiring emulation or a separate runtime process.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 torrent-player | Kotlin
🎯 Primary Use Case: Downloading and streaming torrent files on Android devices with a focus on efficiency and user experience.
✨ Key Features: • Single-Contract Workflow (Magnet/Torrent -> Local Storage -> Stream/Play) • In-Progress Streaming & Per-File Playback • Selective File Downloads • Battery-Friendly & Low-RAM Stability (Native Go engine) • Modern Material 3 Design with Jetpack Compose
📖 Summary: Torrent Player is a native Android application designed for downloading and streaming torrent files efficiently. It offers a user-friendly interface for managing downloads, selecting specific files, and playing content directly within the app or via external players, all while prioritizing battery life and low resource consumption.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 Favnyr | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: A fast, private, and highly configurable file management tool for users who need efficient organization and quick access to their files across different projects and layouts.
✨ Key Features: • Portable single executable • No installer, admin rights, or telemetry • Side-by-side panels (up to 16) • Workspaces for saving panel arrangements • Favorites across workspaces
📖 Summary: Favnyr is a modern, lightweight, and portable file manager for Windows and Linux, built with Rust and Slint. It offers a private-by-construction approach with no network requests, telemetry, or installers, focusing on user control and productivity through features like side-by-side panels, workspaces, and custom commands.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 Telegram-Drive | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide users with a desktop-like file management experience for their Telegram messages and channels, effectively turning their Telegram account into a personal cloud storage drive.
✨ Key Features: • Organize, transfer, preview, stream, sync, and share files • Utilizes Telegram's Saved Messages and channels for storage • Local-first file workspace
📖 Summary: Telegram Drive is an open-source desktop application that transforms your Telegram account into a cloud storage solution. It allows users to organize, transfer, preview, stream, sync, and share files stored in Telegram's Saved Messages and channels, acting as a local-first file workspace.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ hyperframes | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Generating MP4 videos from HTML and CSS code, particularly for use by AI agents to automate video creation.
✨ Key Features: • HTML to Video Rendering • CSS Styling Support • Seekable Animations • CLI Tool • AI Agent Integration (Skills)
📖 Summary: HyperFrames is an open-source framework that converts HTML, CSS, and animations into MP4 videos. It's designed for use with AI coding agents, local CLI, and as a rendering core for authoring workflows.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source
